title: Big four banks pass on rates pain
full_text:
The big four banks have started to pass on higher rates to mortgage holders, a day after the Reserve Bank announced its fifth increase of the year.
On Wednesday, Westpac announced a “difficult” rate rise for customers, saying it would pass on the full rate increase from November 13.“We know another interest rate increase may be difficult for many households, particularly those who have already adjusted their budget this year,” Westpac chief executive, consumer, Carolyn McCann said.
Moments later, National Australia Bank said it would also pass on the full 25-basis-point increase on the same day.
“We know another rate increase will be tough for some homeowners,” NAB Group executive, personal banking, Ana Marinkovic said.
“For customers with a mortgage, these increases add up.
“We’re encouraging people to take a fresh look at their repayments and household budget.” Macquarie Bank was the first lender to lift the cash rate for both mortgage holders and savers alike from November 19, moving immediately after the Reserve Bank’s decision on Tuesday. The RBA announced a further 25-basis-point interest rate increase, taking the official cash rate to 4.85 per cent.
This was the fifth interest rate rise in 2026, following increases in February, March, May and September, taking the cash rate to its highest level since November 2008.
Macquarie head of personal banking Ben Perham said the bank wanted to give a bit of time before passing on the interest rate pain.
“With household budgets already feeling the strain, [Tuesday’s] decision by the RBA will be challenging for many Australians,” Mr Perham said.
“To help our variable home loan customers prepare, we’re again waiting more than two weeks before this latest increase takes effect.
“At the same time, our transaction and savings account customers will see their variable rates increase, with no monthly fees or complex ‘hoops or catches’ to navigate.” Mr Perham urged struggling households to get in contact with bank. “If you are facing financial hardship or are worried about meeting your home loan repayments, please reach out to our specialist team to understand what financial assistance options may be available,” he said.
People under mortgage stress are being urged to negotiate with their bank to try to negotiate a better rate.
Finder home loan expert Richard Whitten said a rate rise would add more pressure to households already feeling the squeeze.
“Since January, the cash rate would have climbed 1.25 percentage points,” he said.
“On a $500,000 mortgage, that’s roughly $258 a month, or $3094 per year more that you’re having to fork out compared to the start of the year – it’s a huge hit to the budget.
“Lenders have been pretty quick to pass on each of these hikes. “If you haven’t already, now is the time to call your bank and ask for a better rate, or compare home loans to see if you could be paying less.”
